domain: Ambient civilian crowd simulation and patrol-civilian interaction (social-force avoidance, graduated threat reaction, pattern-of-life micro-variation) for a deterministic top-down Afghan-valley tactical sim.
paramTargets: PERSONAL SPACE radii (m): intimate/avoid 1.5; tier OBLIVIOUS >45; WARY 30-45; CLEAR-ROAD/move-aside 12-30; FLEE inside dynamic threat ring 8-18 (scaled by armed-count & gunfire). Armed-man berth (social-force) ramp start 14 m, hard push <6 m, strength 1.6-2.4 vs goal. Civ-civ separation 1.8 m. Amble speed: pick a per-civ TECH_SPEED-equivalent 0.7-1.4 m/s (child 0.9-1.6, elder 0.5-0.9); current default 'traveling'=2.0 m/s is ~2x too fast. Dwell at a routine node: 8-40 s. Re-pick errand chance/tick: keep ~0.01 but gate on dwell timer. Curiosity radius (child approach) 18 m, approach-to 4 m; elder withdraw radius 25 m. Reaction hysteresis: tier can rise instantly, decays one step per 2-4 s (panic decay already dt*0.08). Soldier civ-yield: paceScale floor 0.55 when a civ is within 6 m of the wake ahead, interval-keep berth 3 m, never below cohesion floor.
pitfalls: 1) Do NOT add Math.random / Date.now / unsalted sim.rng.next() in civilianBrain for per-civ traits — it breaks replay determinism and (because civilianBrain runs every civ every tick) desyncs. Derive variation from RNG.hashString(u.id) ONCE (cache on the unit) plus sim.timeS for slow phase, never per-tick draws. 2) Do NOT raise SEP_RADIUS globally in steering.ts — soldiers share that path; a big symmetric radius makes the squad file balloon and re-introduces the choke pile-up the wake model just fixed. Add an ASYMMETRIC armed-berth as a separate civilian-only steering term or as a goal-direction bias inside civilianBrain, so the civ yields but the soldier doesn't get shoved. 3) The fear loop already scans ALL effects and ALL units per civ per tick — do NOT add a second O(units) scan per tier. Reuse the single neighbor pass; pull armed-men via the existing spatial grid (neighborsFor-style bucket query), not a full sim.units loop. 4) Civilians go through moveUnit→steer already, so they will NOT interpenetrate soldiers IF given a path; a civ standing still (path=[]) is NOT steered — a halted civ can be walked through. Give a wary/move-aside civ a short sidestep path so separation actually runs. 5) Don't let the soldier civ-yield call sim.pathTo/re-path — only modulate nav.paceScale (read u.path/wake), or you reset the stall watchdog and stall the patrol. 6) Don't flip stance every tick (jitter) — debounce stance with the existing brainTimer/hysteresis. 7) reachablePoint/civSafePoint snapping is mandatory on every civ destination (sidesteps included) or you reintroduce the 470 ms cross-river free-A* tick stall.

principles.title: Replace the binary panic gate with 4 graduated reaction tiers
principles.realityOrCraft: Real villagers near a patrol don't toggle calm↔sprint. They notice (look up), assess, then either keep working, drift to the field edge, clear the track and stand aside, or — only at gunfire/very-close armed men — bolt. The tier is a continuous read of threat proximity & intensity, not one flag.
principles.currentGap: civilian.ts:civilianBrain — single threshold `if (u.panic > 0.3)` (line 36) splits the entire behavior into amble vs flee. There is no wary/move-aside state; a civ either ignores armed men completely or runs.
principles.change: Compute a `threat` scalar per tick from (a) nearest-armed-man distance, (b) count of armed men within 45 m, (c) gunfire/blast fear already summed. Map to tier via thresholds with rising-instant / falling-slow hysteresis (store u.reactTier on the unit). OBLIVIOUS: run existing calm routine. WARY: stop walking, stance 'stand', faceLock toward nearest armed man (watch), small dwell. CLEAR-ROAD: compute a sidestep target = current pos pushed perpendicular off the patrol's line of travel to the nearest field edge / ≥12 m off the armed man's bearing, civMoveTo it, then hold facing the patrol. FLEE: existing flee block. Keep u.panic but make it ONE input to the tier, not the switch.
principles.params: OBLIVIOUS threat<0.15 (no armed man <45 m); WARY 0.15-0.35 (armed man 30-45 m); CLEAR-ROAD 0.35-0.6 (armed man 12-30 m OR on patrol path); FLEE >0.6 (gunfire near, or armed man <12 m, or panic>0.45). Tier rises same tick, falls one step / 2.5 s. threat = clamp01( 0.6*(1-nearArmed/45) + 0.25*min(armedCount,3)/3 + fear ).
principles.risk: Over-eager CLEAR-ROAD could make a whole bazaar scatter off-road and read as 'they all know'. Verify with scripts/civ-live.ts + a new metric (mean tier per civ over a normal patrol pass) — most civs should sit OBLIVIOUS/WARY; only the few within 30 m clear. Adjust the 0.35 threshold if too many clear.

principles.title: Add an asymmetric armed-man social-force berth so civilians give soldiers room (and stop clipping through them)
principles.realityOrCraft: Pedestrians keep a personal-space bubble that is much larger toward an armed/authority figure than toward each other; the avoidance is asymmetric — the civilian yields, the soldier holds his line (escalation-of-force feel).
principles.currentGap: steering.ts uses one symmetric SEP_RADIUS=2.4 m for everyone (line 39); civilians barely avoid soldiers and a HALTED civ (path=[]) is never steered, so soldiers walk through standing villagers. There is no larger berth for armed men.
principles.change: In civilianBrain, before issuing/keeping a calm path, compute a repulsion vector from armed men within ARMED_BERTH and blend it into the civ's goal direction (deterministic, no RNG): dir = norm(goalDir + sum over armed men of away*strength*falloff). This biases the existing civMoveTo target sideways so the civ arcs around the patrol. Crucially, when a WARY/CLEAR civ would otherwise stand still inside the berth, give it a 2-4 m sidestep path so moveUnit→steer actually runs and resolves the overlap. Keep civ-civ separation in steering.ts but consider lowering civilian-civilian SEP to ~1.8 m (villagers cluster tighter than a squad). Do NOT widen the global SEP_RADIUS.
principles.params: ARMED_BERTH 14 m ramp, falloff (1-d/14)^2, hard term inside 6 m. strength 1.8 (cap blended turn so the civ still makes progress on errands). Sidestep magnitude 3 m perpendicular to the armed man's bearing, snapped via reachablePoint+civSafePoint. Civ-civ SEP_RADIUS branch 1.8 m.
principles.risk: Blending too hard makes civs orbit soldiers / never reach errands. Cap the steering turn (e.g. clamp blend so |turn|<60°). Verify no new strand: re-run scripts/civ-live.ts (arrived count must not drop) and watch for civ tick-time regressions (the berth scan must use the spatial grid, not a full units loop).

principles.title: Acknowledge civilians from the soldier side: ease the patrol pace when a civ is on the wake ahead (EOF feel) without breaking cohesion
principles.realityOrCraft: A patrol bearing down on a farmer on the track slows and lets him clear — wave-through / escalation-of-force. It does not barge through or break formation; the point man just eases the throttle.
principles.currentGap: No file touches civilians from the friendly side. The pace governor in formation.ts steerSquad sets nav.paceScale purely from squad lag (lines 163-165); friendly.ts never references civilians. Soldiers march into villagers at full pace.
principles.change: In formation.ts steerSquad, after computing the lag-based paceScale, query civilians (via the sim's civilian list / spatial grid) within a short cone ahead of the navigator along headDir. If a civ is within CIV_YIELD_DIST of the wake ahead, take paceScale = min(paceScale, CIV_YIELD_FLOOR). This is pure throttle — no re-path, no formation change — so cohesion and the stall watchdog are untouched. Optionally nudge the nav's local steering to keep CIV_BERTH off the civ (the existing steer() separation already does most of this since civs are non-hostile neighbors).
principles.params: Cone: civ within 8 m of the path ahead AND within 14 m forward, |bearing|<45°. CIV_YIELD_FLOOR 0.55 (matches the existing cohesion floor, so it never dead-stops). CIV_BERTH 3 m. Clear the yield the moment no civ is in the cone (instant resume).
principles.risk: A village full of civs could chronically throttle a patrol to 0.55 and look timid / arrive late. Gate the yield to OBLIVIOUS/WARY civs only (a fleeing civ is already clearing) and to non-contact (expectContact false). Verify squad arrival time in scripts/squad-arrival.ts doesn't regress past the tactical window through a populated village.

principles.title: Per-civ pace, dwell, and a calm idle so movement reads organic instead of a 2 m/s shuffle
principles.realityOrCraft: Villagers move at walking pace (~1.1-1.4 m/s), kids dart faster, elders shuffle slower, and people STOP — they work a field, water animals, chat — for tens of seconds, not glide continuously. Variation is per-person and stable.
principles.currentGap: techniqueOf() defaults civilians to 'traveling' = 2.0 m/s (combat.ts:121,304) — a brisk march for everyone, identical. civilianBrain re-picks a routine node on a flat 1% chance with no dwell (lines 68-74), so civs either glide nonstop or stand dead. No per-civ trait.
principles.change: Derive a stable per-civ trait set ONCE from RNG.hashString(u.id) (cache fields on the Unit at makeCivilian time in entities.ts, or lazily in civilianBrain guarded by a cached flag): paceBias, dwellBias, curiosity. Set the civ's effective amble speed by giving it paceScale = paceBias (the integrator already multiplies speed by paceScale) while keeping technique 'patrol' (1.5 m/s) instead of 'traveling' — net amble ~0.7-1.4 m/s. On reaching a routine node, set a dwell timer (u.brainTimer) of dwellBias seconds during which the civ holds (path=[], stance 'stand', small facing drift) before the next errand re-pick. Add a slow per-civ facing wander (sin(timeS*0.2 + hashPhase)) while idle so a standing villager isn't a frozen statue.
principles.params: paceBias 0.7-1.4 (child 0.9-1.6, elder 0.5-0.9) from hash. Set civ technique 'patrol' (1.5) so paceScale*1.5 lands in walking range. dwellBias 8-40 s (elders longer, kids shorter). Idle facing wander ±25° at 0.2 rad/s. All from hash(u.id), zero per-tick RNG.
principles.risk: Caching traits must not vary by call order; compute purely from u.id hash so it's deterministic regardless of tick. Verify replay determinism with the existing balance/smoke seeds (scripts/smoke.ts) — two runs of the same seed must produce identical civ positions. If technique change affects LOS/stealth, re-check civ visibility tests.

principles.title: Role-flavored curiosity: children approach the patrol, elders withdraw, women/farmers keep working
principles.realityOrCraft: In a real valley the patrol draws kids who run alongside and stare; elders and women pointedly turn away and go inside; working-age men keep a wary distance. This single behavioral split is what makes the crowd read as people, not particles.
principles.currentGap: civilian.ts treats all roles identically — Role ('farmer','herder','villager','child','elder') is never read in the brain. Everyone reacts the same to a patrol.
principles.change: In the WARY/CLEAR tier branch of civilianBrain, branch on u.role: CHILD with curiosity>0.5 and panic<0.2 → set destination toward the nearest soldier (approach to ~4 m, then orbit/dwell) instead of clearing — a deterministic 'approach' using the armed man's pos, gated so it never enters FLEE. ELDER → bias the clear-road target toward home/compound (homePoint) and stand facing away (withdraw). FARMER/HERDER → mostly stay on the field node (higher OBLIVIOUS threshold, keep working) and only clear if the patrol comes very close. VILLAGER → neutral wary watch. Make curiosity a hashed trait so only SOME kids approach.
principles.params: Child approach radius 18 m, stop at 4 m, only if curiosity (hash) >0.5 and threat<0.6. Elder withdraw radius 25 m, retreat toward homePoint. Farmer OBLIVIOUS threshold raised +0.1 (works through closer). Curiosity 0-1 from hash(u.id+'cur').
principles.risk: Kids approaching armed men + the civClear fire-discipline check could create awkward 'civilian in the line of fire' situations; ensure approaching kids still flee instantly at FLEE tier (gunfire). Verify no friendly-fire civCasualty regression in a contact scenario (scripts/realism-probe.ts or a contact seed).

principles.title: Bearing-optimal, de-conflicted assignment for the 360° security halt so men don't cross the circle through each other
principles.realityOrCraft: When a squad sets up all-round security it does NOT have each man walk to a fixed compass slot — each man takes the SECTOR HE'S ALREADY NEAREST and settles outward, so nobody crosses the center or shoulders through a buddy.
principles.currentGap: formation.ts holdSecurity (lines 225-239) lays men by RAW member index: a=(i/n)*2π+0.4. A man at the south can be assigned the north slot and is told to walk straight across the ring through everyone — the user-flagged 'stuck on each other' setup. No assignment, no de-confliction.
principles.change: Rewrite holdSecurity to (1) generate n outward ring slots, (2) assign each man to a slot by his CURRENT bearing from center (sort men by atan2(pos-center), sort slots by angle, match in order — an O(n log n) rotation-aligned assignment that gives each man the nearest free sector and prevents crossings), and (3) keep faceLock = slot bearing (face out). Optionally snap each slot toward the nearest cover within a small radius (coverAt) for believability. Men already in their sector (dist<2) get path=[] so they settle smoothly instead of re-planning. Steering separation (already active) then resolves the last meter without piling.
principles.params: Assign by sorting both men and slots by angle from center and rotating the slot list to minimize total angular travel (try all n rotations, pick min sum |Δangle| — n≤12 so it's trivial). Slot radius = passed radius; cover-snap search 3 m; settle threshold 2 m; keep clamp to worldSize-4.
principles.risk: Angular-rotation match is O(n^2) worst case but n≤12 so negligible. Risk: if two men start at the same bearing they could still contend — the existing steer() separation handles the final meter. Verify with scripts/cohesion.ts (heading jitter on halt) and a screenshot of a security halt before/after; men should fan to nearest sectors with no center-crossing.
